blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Knowledge graph-to-text (KG-to-text) generation verbalizes a set of knowledge graph triples into fluent natural language. While fine-tuned encoder-decoder models have long been the standard approach, recent LLMs are becoming increasingly competitive. We benchmark recent LLMs against fine-tuned encoder-decoder models, using reference-based metrics and graph-grounded reference-free LLM-based evaluation validated against human annotations. We observed that recent LLMs substantially narrow, and in several settings close, the gap with fine-tuned models on reference-based metrics, while performing better on graph-grounded metrics. LLM-based evaluation scores show limited correlation with reference-based metrics, suggesting that the two approaches capture different aspects of generation quality. Graph-grounded evaluation reveals that prompted models produce fewer contradictions and triple omissions than fine-tuned models, and these errors increase more rapidly with graph size for fine-tuned models, highlighting differences between the two approaches that reference-based metrics may not fully capture.
blocks.zh: 知识图对文本(KG-to-text)生成将一组知识图对三进制成流畅的自然语言. 虽然经过微调的编码器-解码器模型长期以来一直是标准方法,但最近的有限责任公司越来越具有竞争力。 我们以微调编码器-解码器模型为基准,使用基于参考的衡量尺度和基于图表的无参考LLM评价,对照人类说明加以验证。 我们注意到,最近的有限责任管理办法大大缩小了与参照度量衡的微调模型的差距,并在一些环境下缩小了这种差距,同时在以图表为基础的度量衡上表现较好。 基于LLM的评价分数显示与基于参考的衡量标准的相关性有限,表明这两种方法捕捉到生成质量的不同方面. 以图表为基础的评价显示,与微调模型相比,被激发模型产生的矛盾和三重遗漏较少,这些错误随着微调模型的图表大小而增加得更快,凸显了基于参考的衡量标准可能无法完全捕捉到的两种方法之间的差异.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Knowledge Graphs store information in the form of structured triples as (subject, relation, object). The task of verbalising the knowledge graphs into natural language sentences is a significant and well-studied problem within the natural language generation domain. With the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs), it is important to understand how effectively recent models perform this task. In this paper advances the evaluation of recent pre-trained models on graph-to-text benchmark datasets, We investigate the performance of five recent model families spanning diverse architectures: dense decoder-only (Gemma-4-E4B-it, Gemma-4-31B-it, Team et al. (2026) , Granite-4.2 IBM Research (2026) ), mixture-of-experts (Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it Team et al. (2026) , Nemotron-3 Blakeman et al. (2025) ), encoder-decoder (T5-Gemma2 Zhang et al. (2025) ), closed sourced GPT-5 Singh et al. (2025) on the following knowledge graph datasets: WebNLG17 Gardent et al. (2017) , WebNLG20 Ferreira et al. (2020) (English subset), and DART Nan et al. (2021) . For evaluating the performance of KG-to-Text generation systems, the most commonly used metrics are reference-based like BLEU, METEOR, ChrF++, and BLEURT. However, BLEU Papineni et al. (2002) , METEOR Banerjee and Lavie (2005) , and ChrF++ Popović (2017) judge the generated text based on surface similarity to the reference text and do not evaluate its semantic meaningfulness. BLEURT Sellam et al. (2020) , on the other hand, is a learned metric designed to mimic human evaluation. Additionally, we have found that different researchers use different sets and implementations of metrics, which makes it difficult to compare the results with the published State-of-The-Art (SoTA) approaches. Therefore, we have used an elaborate set of metrics consisting of BLEU, METEOR, ChrF++, Rouge-L, BLEURT, BERTScore Zhang et al. (2019) , BARTScore Yuan et al. (2021) , and PARENT Dhingra et al. (2019) and have categorized them into three different categories based on the function of the metrics. Additionally, we have also studied LLMs as judge category of metrics as source- grounded or reference-free judges and explored how useful and reliable these metrics can be for evaluating LLM-generated text in terms of criteria that cannot be explicitly judged by the standard NLG metrics. We frame the following research questions on the benchmark datasets and try to find the answers: RQ1. Under one scoring pipeline with a multi-reference protocol, where do recent prompted LLMs (GPT-5 mini, Gemma-4-31B, Granite-4.2-30B, Nemotron-3-Ultra) and a LoRA-adapted Hu et al. (2021) encoder-decoder (T5-Gemma2) model stand against fully fine-tuned T5-large, per metric and per dataset? RQ2. Do the reference-based metric families agree with one another and with a source-grounded judge on these LLM generated outputs? RQ3. What does an LLM judge measure on KG-to-text outputs, when two different LLM judges are compared and validated against human annotation? RQ4. Do fine-tuned and prompted systems make the same kind of errors? Our contributions are: 1) a unified evaluation of five recent model families against fine-tuned T5-large on three benchmarks with eight reference-based metrics, showing that compared with earlier published zero-shot results the gap has narrowed from tens of BLEU points to a few, with parity on neural metrics and a remaining lead for fine-tuning on BLEU, BARTScore and PARENT scores (RQ1); 2) an analysis of metric agreement showing that the reference-based families agree among themselves and not very strongly with a source-grounded judge (RQ2); 3) a two-judge BinEval Cho et al. (2026) evaluation of all outputs, validated against 220 human-labelled outputs (two model outputs on the same 110 graphs) with adjudicated error types, establishing that the LLM judges reproduce human omission labels triple by triple and detect contradictions and entity corruptions, and that they do not detect unsupported elaboration (RQ3); 4) the finding that, by the human standard, the fine-tuned and the prompted systems have a faithfulness problem in a similar share of outputs but of different kinds: corruption and omission against elaboration(RQ4).

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
The early efforts for verbalizing structured data relied on recurrent neural network (RNN) architectures, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models, to encode graph-derived sequences and generate natural language descriptions Song et al. (2018) ; Zhao et al. (2020) ; Guo et al. (2020) . Subsequently, Graph Neural Networks (GNN) based models have been employed to use a graph encoder to better capture the structural dependencies and relational information inherent in graph data; Li et al. (2021) and Koncel-Kedziorski et al. (2019) .
More recent approaches, however, have increasingly shifted towards the use of large pre-trained language models, often relying on linearized graph representations as textual input sequences. Recent work has explored both pre-trained sequence-to-sequence architectures Ribeiro et al. (2021) ; Li et al. (2024) and open-source generative language models He et al. (2025) , Iarosh et al. (2025) . The implementations of Ribeiro et al. (2021) based on T5 and BART are widely adopted as benchmark baselines for KG-to-Text evaluation. We have used WebNLG17, WebNLG20 and DART as the benchmark datasets. The main reason for choosing these datasets is that they have negligible graph-text alignment noise in their training data i.e. each triple from the graph is described in the corresponding text and there is no information in the text which is not grounded in the corresponding graphs. This property is missing in most of the other KG-to-Text datasets available. For example, GraphNarrative Shi et al. (2023) dataset has on an average 0.62 hallucinated entities and 0.74 hallucinated relations per graph-text pairs, EventNarrative Colas et al. (2021) has on an average 0.69 hallucinated entities and 0.70 hallucinated relations, TEKGEN Agarwal et al. (2021) has these numbers as 0.84 hallucinated entities and 0.92 hallucinated relations by construction He et al. (2025) . Another dataset GenWiki Jin et al. (2020) has 58.1% unused triplets and 65.1% unguessable text in the graphs and corresponding text, respectively Kim et al. (2026) . While the models finetuned on the respective datasets have consistently achieved higher performance on structured data; Li et al. (2024) and Yuan and Färber (2023) explored closed-source generative models for generating text from GPT-3 in a zero-shot scenario. Their results showed that the generative models without any fine-tuning fall significantly behind the fine-tuned sequence-to-sequence architectures. Recently, Iarosh et al. (2025) evaluated GPT-4o in zero-shot and chain-of-thought (CoT) few-shot settings on WebNLG20 and reported significant performance gains when using detailed prompts. Building on these findings, our work extends the evaluation to a broader set of recent LLM architectures. Evaluation of graph-to-text systems has traditionally relied on reference-based metrics and on human annotation of dimensions such as triple coverage and hallucination. Because human annotation is costly to scale, recent work has turned to LLM-based judges as an automatic alternative Liu et al. (2023) . Rather than asking an LLM for a single holistic rating, CheckEval Lee et al. (2025) and BinEval Cho et al. (2026) decompose the judgment into a set of binary questions and aggregate the verdicts. A related line of work localises data-text mismatches (omitted, extra and incorrect content), but does so with a fine-tuned verifier rather than LLM prompting Efimov-Zhang et al. (2026) . Huidrom et al. (2025) , on the other hand, meta-evaluate 29 reference-free metrics against human semantic-consistency ratings on WebNLG. For this study, we have included BinEval and GPTScore Fu et al. (2024) in our evaluation protocol.
blocks.zh:
早期对结构化数据的语音化工作依赖于经常性神经网络(RNN)架构,包括长期短期内存(LSTM)和Gated Central Unit(GRU)模型,以编码出图表出自序列并生成自然语言描述 Song等 (2018); Zhao等 (2020); Guo等 (2020). 随后,Graph Neural Networks(GNN)基于图表的模型被应用来使用图表编码器来更好地捕捉图表数据所固有的结构依赖性和关系信息;Li等 (2021)和Koncel-Kedziorski等 (2019).
然而,较新的方法已日益转向使用经过预先训练的大型语言模型,往往依靠线性化的图示作为文字输入序列. 最近的工作探索了预先训练的序列至序列架构Ribeiro等人(2021年);Li等人(2024年)和开源基因语言模型。 He等 (2025)., Iarosh等 (2025). 基于T5和BART的Ribeiro等人(2021年)的实施被广泛作为KG到Text评价的基准基线. 我们使用WebNLG17,WebNLG20和DART作为基准数据集. 选择这些数据集的主要原因是,它们在其训练数据中有可忽略不计的图文本对齐噪声,即从图中取出的每一个三分点在相应的文本中被描述,文本中没有任何信息不以相应的图表为基础. 此属性在大多数可用的 KG 到 Text 数据集中缺失 。 例如,图表 Shi等人(2023年)的数据集平均有0.62个幻觉实体和0.74个幻觉关系,每对图文对应,EventNarrative Colas等人(2021年)平均有0.69个幻觉实体和0.70个幻觉关系,TEKGEN Agarwal等人(2021年)的数字为0.84个幻觉实体和0.92个幻觉关系,由Building He等人(2025年). 另一个数据集GenWiki Jin等人(2020年)在图表和对应文本中分别有58.1%的未使用三胞胎和65.1%的可忽略文本(2026年). 虽然对各自数据集进行微调的模型在结构化数据上一直取得了较高的性能;而Li等人(2024年)和Yuan和Färber(2023年)则探索了从GPT-3生成文本的闭源基因模型,在零镜头的情景下. 他们的结果显示,未作任何微调的基因模型大大落后于被微调的序列到序列架构. 最近,Iarosh等人(2025年)在WebNLG20上对GPT-4o进行零镜头和多镜头(COT)链式设定评价,并在使用详细提示时报告了显著的性能提高. 在这些结论的基础上,我们的工作将评价工作扩大到一系列更广泛的近期的LLM架构。 对从图表到文本系统的评价历来依靠基于参考的衡量尺度和对维度的人类注释,如三重覆盖和幻觉等. 由于人类注解的规模代价高昂,最近的工作已转向基于LLM的法官,作为刘等的自动替代(2023年). CheckEval Lee等人(2025年)和BinEval Cho等人(2026年)没有要求LLM进行单一的整体评级,而是将判决分解为一组二进制问题并汇总判决. 相关的一行工作将数据-文本不匹配(输入,额外和不正确的内容)本地化,但使用微调的验证器而不是LLM来提示Efimov-Zhang等(2026). Huidrom等 (2025) 另一方面,元评价了在WebNLG上针对人类语义-一致性收视率的29个无参考量度. 就这项研究而言,我们已经将BinEval和GPTScore Fu等人(2024年)列入我们的评价议定书。

blocks.en: 3 Datasets
blocks.zh: 3个数据集

blocks.en:
Below, we describe these datasets in detail: WebNLG17 . This dataset consists of RDF triples and their corresponding text descriptions released as part of the WebNLG challenge, with the goal of producing a common benchmark to compare “microplanners” for RDF description Gardent et al. (2017) . It has become an important benchmark for KG-to-text generation. The dataset contains graphs having 1 to 7 triples, which are verbalized into a few sentences. All the experiments mentioned in this paper have been performed on the full test subset of the WebNLG17 dataset. WebNLG20 .WebNLG dataset has been revised a few times since the first challenge Gardent et al. (2017) . The WebNLG20 Ferreira et al. (2020) dataset has a new category called "company" along with all the categories present in the WebNLG17 version. Consistent with the previous dataset, all the experiments on this dataset have been performed on the full test dataset. DART . DART Nan et al. (2021) is a large open domain graph to text dataset constructed using various sources: human annotation on
Wikipedia tables from WikiSQL Zhong et al. (2017) and WikiTableQuestions Pasupat and Liang (2015) ; automatic conversion of questions in WikiSQL into declarative sentences; and inclusion of RDF to text datasets WebNLG 2017 and E2E Dušek et al. (2018) . DART thus has triples sourced from diverse domains and serves as a benchmark dataset for graph-to-text generation.

blocks.en: 4 Model Architectures
blocks.zh: 4个示范建筑

blocks.en: The set of model architectures we selected provides checkpoints ranging from 270M-parameter encoder-decoder models to a 550B-parameter sparse model. The architectural difference among these models can be stated as: Encoder-decoder vs decoder-only . We have two models with encoder-decoder architecture, T5 and T5-Gemma2. However, the later is an encoder-decoder model which adapts a pretrained decoder-only Gemma 3 model into an encoder-decoder, and adds tied word embeddings across encoder and decoder and a merged attention module that unifies decoder self- and cross-attention. We use the 270M-270M, 1B-1B and 4B-4B checkpoints. All other models have decoder-only architectures. Dense vs Sparse. Granite-4.2 (with size variants 3B, 8B and 30B) is fully dense decoder-only model. Gemma-4 has size variants 4B-it, 26B-A4B and 31B-it; of which 4B-it and 31B-it are dense decoder-only models whereas 26B-A4B is a mixture-of-experts Shazeer et al. (2017) model with around 26 billion total parameters and 4 billion active parameters with 128 experts and uses interleaved local sliding-window and global attention. The three Nemotron-3 models are sparse with Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B having approximately 3 billion active parameters out of total 30 billion parameters; Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B having 12 billion parameters out of 120 billion total parameters and Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B having 55 billion active parameters out of the total 550 billion parameters and uses interleaved Mamba-2 state-space Dao and Gu (2024) and MoE layers, with a few self-attention layers. Open vs closed source models . Out of all the models that we are using, GPT-5’s architecture is undisclosed, so it serves as the closed-source reference. We employed three variants of GPT-5: GPT-5-nano, GPT-5-mini, and the full GPT-5 model.

blocks.en: 5 Experiments
blocks.zh: 5个实验

blocks.en: 5.1 Fine-tuned models
blocks.zh: 5.1 微调型号

blocks.en: We adopted Shi et al. (2023) ’s pipeline for fine-tuning T5 for all our T5 experiments. We fine-tuned the different variants of T5 (Small, Base and Large) on the three datasets WebNLG17, WebNLG20 and DART independently, using a learning rate of 3e-5, a batch size of 8 (for training and validation sets), for up to 30 epochs with early stopping (patience of 3) based on validation performance. Source and target sequences are truncated/padded to a maximum length of 384 tokens for both training and generation, with beam search decoding with a beam size of 3 used at inference. The implementation uses linearized knowledge graphs by representing their triples as a sequence of subject–predicate–object elements, concatenated in a fixed order and separated by special delimiter tokens "<H>", "<R>" and "<T>". Training was run on a single A40/A6000 GPU per model. We fine-tuned T5Gemma2 (4B-4B variant) for the knowledge-graph-to-text generation task using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). blocks.en: 5.2 Prompted models
blocks.zh: 5.2 快速型号

blocks.en: For all the decoder-only models and GPT-5, we have used few-shot prompting. In our experiments on these models, following the methodology of Yuan and Färber (2023) , each test instance was treated as a separate request, and the model’s output was recorded as the generated text. Instead of using the simple prompt, "generate text from graph," we utilized a more elaborate prompt as shown in Table 10 . The prompt was inspired by the mistakes noticed when we used the simple prompt, as mentioned in Appendix A , and it is kept the same for all the models. We provide the input graphs to the models as a text sequence, we have used the same linearization as used in the case of the T5 and T5-Gemma-2 experiment. Given that most of the open-sourced LLMs we used are reasoning or thinking models, we set the thinking or reasoning level to "off" or "none" and similarly for GPT-5 we kept reasoning level to “minimal” . We also set temperature = 0.0, max tokens = 384 and default top-p value wherever applicable. We conducted preliminary experiments with GPT-5-mini and Gemma-4-E4B-it on WebNLG test dataset under different few-shot settings to determine the most suitable k k -shot value for the remaining experiments. For selecting few-shot samples, we first use E5-base-V2 Wang et al. (2022) to obtain dense embeddings of the graph linearizations. This model provides an effective balance between retrieval quality and computational efficiency. Each graph was linearized into a flat textual sequence by concatenating the head, relation, and tail tokens of all triples. To mitigate the risk of data leakage, all samples identical to test instances were removed from the training set. For deciding the best sample retrieval strategy, we selected samples for few-shots based on the cosine similarity between the linearized graph embeddings of the test input and the graphs in training set. As He et al. (2025) mentioned the effectiveness of Difficulty and Diversity of the chosen few shots; we tried Maximal Marginal Relevance Carbonell and Goldstein (1998) as a strategy to balance relevance and non-redundancy in our initial experiments. And as an alternative, we also tried organising both the training and test sets into subsets based on graph triple size. For one-shot retrieval, examples were selected from the subset containing graphs with the same number of triples n n as the test instance. For two-shot retrieval, examples were selected from the n n and n + 1 n+1 triple subsets, while for three-shot retrieval, examples were drawn from the n − 1 n-1 , n n , and n + 1 n+1 triple subsets to introduce structural diversity among the retrieved examples. For test instances belonging to the largest triple-size category, where an n + 1 n+1 subset was unavailable, retrieval was restricted to n n triple subset. We discuss the effectiveness of these retrieval strategies in Section 6.1 .
blocks.zh: 对于所有解码器的模型和GPT-5,我们使用了很少的镜头提示. 在我们对这些模型的实验中,遵循了袁和法尔伯(2023年)的方法,每个测试实例都被作为单独的请求,模型的输出被记录为生成的文本. 我们没有使用简单的“由图表生成的文本”,而是使用了表10所示的更为细致的提示。 如附录A所提到,我们使用简单提示时注意到的错误启发了这个提示,而且对所有模型都保持不变。 我们把输入图作为文本序列提供给模型,我们采用了与T5和T5-Gemma-2实验中所使用的相同的线性化. 鉴于我们所使用的大多数开源的LLMs是推理或思维模型,我们把思维或推理级别设定为"off"或"noone",同样对于GPT-5,我们把推理级别保持为"最小". 我们还设置了温度=0.0,最大符号=384,并在适用的情况下设置了默认的顶p值. 我们在WebNLG测试数据集中进行了GPT-5-mini和Gemma-4-E4B-it的初步实验,在不同的几发设置下确定其余实验最合适的克-射值. 为了选择几发样本,我们首先使用E5-base-V2 Wang等(2022)来得到图示线性化的密集嵌入. 这个模型在检索质量和计算效率之间提供了有效的平衡. 每个图被线化成平坦的文字序列,通过将所有三相的头部,关系,和尾部符号相接而来. 为了减少数据泄露的风险,所有与测试情况相同的样本都从培训中取出。 为了决定最佳的取样策略,我们根据测试输入的线性化图嵌入与训练集中图表的同位素相似性,选择了几发取样. 正如He等(2025年)提到所选择的几发子弹的难度和多样性的有效性;我们尝试了最大边际相关性碳ell和Goldstein(1998年),作为在我们最初的实验中平衡相关性和不重复性的战略. 作为一种替代方案,我们还尝试了组织培训和测试 组合成基于图三大小的子集。 对于一发取回,从包含图的子集中选择了实例,与测试实例的三相nn相同. 对于两发取回,从n和n+1 n+1 三发取回子集中选择了实例,而对于三发取回,则从n−1 n 1 n n 和n+1 n+1 三发取回子集中取出实例,在所取取取的例子中引入结构多样性. 对于属于最大三相大小类的测试实例,如果一个n+1 n+1子集不可用,则检索仅限于nn 三相子集. 我们在第6.1节讨论了这些检索战略的有效性。

blocks.en: 5.3 Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: 5.3 评价议定书

blocks.en: We evaluate the model outputs from multiple perspectives using a diverse set of evaluation metrics. Based on their underlying methodology, these metrics are categorized into four groups. 1) Surface-Level Metrics. These metrics evaluate the generated text based on its lexical overlap with the reference text. The metrics included in this category are BLEU Papineni et al. (2002) , ChrF++ Popović (2017) , METEOR Banerjee and Lavie (2005) , and ROUGE-L Lin (2004) .We compute corpus-level BLEU and chrF++ scores using the SacreBLEU Post (2018) library. METEOR is computed using the implementation provided in NLTK, while ROUGE-L is computed using the rouge-score package. 2) Semantic or Neural Metrics. These metrics assess the semantic similarity and coherence between the generated text and the reference text, going beyond exact lexical matching. The metrics used in this category include BLEURT Sellam et al. (2020) , BERTScore Zhang et al. (2019) , and BARTScore Yuan et al. (2021) . We compute BERTScore using the bert-base-uncased checkpoint, BLEURT using the BLEURT-20 checkpoint, and BARTScore using the facebook/bart-large-cnn checkpoint. 3) Alignment-Based Metrics. When evaluating Large Language Models for graph-to-text generation, it is essential to determine whether the generated text remains grounded in the source graph. The PARENT Dhingra et al. (2019) metric addresses this aspect by computing an F1-based score that measures the alignment of the generated text not only with the reference text but also with the source graph. We adopt a multi-reference evaluation protocol for all metrics. For corpus-level metrics such as BLEU and ChrF++, we use SacreBLEU’s native multi-reference evaluation, where each prediction is evaluated against all available references jointly. For sentence-level metrics, including METEOR, ROUGE-L, BLEURT, BARTScore, and PARENT, scores are computed against each reference independently, and the maximum score across references is retained for each instance. 4) LLM as Judge In the task of Graph-to-Text generation, it is very important to judge the outputs explicitly for the faithfulness to the source graph, the coverage of information present in the graph and the fluency of the text as a whole. We leverage LLMs as judges in this task through BinEval Cho et al. (2026) and GPTScore Fu et al. (2024) . BinEval is a training-free, reference-free framework that decomposes each evaluation criterion into atomic yes/no questions rather than asking an LLM for one holistic score. A meta-prompt first generates the atomic questions from the task prompt, organised by evaluation dimension. An evaluator LLM then checks the output against the source for each question, returning a binary verdict and a short natural-language explanation. The verdicts are aggregated into a score per dimension, so a low score can be traced to the specific failed checks. We evaluated Faithfulness to graph, graph triple Coverage and Fluency of the model outputs using BinEval framework. We use DeepSeekV-4.1-Flash Xu et al. (2026) and GLM-5.3-Flash GLM-5-Team et al. (2026) with thinking disabled as the judge LLMs. Instead of allowing the BinEval framework to generate binary questions, we provided our own questions for each criterion to the judge LLMs. For each question, the evaluator gives binary output and the final recorded scores are the mean of the total satisfied questions per dimension in the case of Faithfulness and Fluency. The questions provided to the judges are presented in Tables 12 and 13 . For Coverage, the final score is the ratio of the sum of the binary score for each triple to the total triples. GPTScore is also a reference-free metric that scores a generated text by the likelihood a pretrained language model assigns to it, conditioned on an instruction. We use GPTScore to get the likelihood of the generated output given the source graph and task instruction. The official implementation of GPTScore is tested with Flan-T5, GPT-2, GPT-3 and OPT family models, however, we have used DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in non-thinking setting as it is a more recent model and belongs to a different model family compared to the LLMs we are using for text generation. The implementation details for both BinEval and GPTScore are in Appendix B .
blocks.zh: 我们利用一套不同的评价指标,从多个角度评价模型产出。 根据其基本方法,这些衡量标准分为四组。 (1) 地表测量。 这些衡量标准根据生成的文本与参考文本的词汇重叠来评价所生成的文本. 列入这一类别的衡量标准是:BLEU Papineni等人(2002年)、ChrF++ Popović(2017年)、METEOR Banerjee和Lavie(2005年)和ROUGE-L L Lin(2004年)。 我们使用 SacreBleU Post (2018) 库计算BLEU和chrF++的分数。 METEOR是使用NLTK提供的执行计算,而ROUGE-L是使用rouge-score包计算。 2) 语义或神经计量. 这些衡量标准评估了生成的文本与参考文本之间的语义相似性和一致性,超越了精确的词汇匹配. 这一类别中使用的度量衡包括BLEURT Sellam等人(2020年)、BERTScore Zhang等人(2019年)和BARTScore Yuan等人(2021年)。 我们使用Bert-base-uncase的检查站计算BERTScore,使用BLEURT-20检查站计算BLEURT,使用BARTScore,使用facebook/bart-mall-cnn检查站计算BERTScore。 3) 对齐计量。 在对大语言模型进行图到文本生成的评价时,必须确定生成的文本是否仍以出自源图为基础. PENT Dhingra等人(2019年)的衡量标准通过计算一个基于F1的分数来解决这个方面,该分数衡量生成的文本不仅与参考文本一致,而且与源图一致. 我们通过了所有衡量标准的多参考评价协议。 对于BLEU和ChrF++等生物体层面的衡量标准,我们使用SacreBLEU的本土多参考评价,在这种评价中,每个预测都与所有可用的参考数据进行联合评价。 对于包括METEOR、ROUGE-L、BLEURT、BARTScore和PANT在内的句子级衡量标准,根据每个参考标准分别计算分数,并保留每个参考标准的最大分数。 (4) LLM担任法官 在"图对图"生成的任务中,必须明确判断产出是否忠实于出处图,图中信息覆盖度和整个文本的流畅度. 我们通过BinEval Cho等人(2026年)和GPTScore Fu等人(2024年)利用法学硕士作为法官执行这项任务。 BinEval是一个没有训练,没有参考的框架,它将每个评价标准分解为原子是/否问题,而不是要求一个LLM来获得一个整体分数. 元瞬间首先从任务提示中产生原子问题,由评价层面组织. 然后,一名评价员LLM对照每个问题的来源检查产出,返回一个二进制判断和一个简短的自然语言解释. 判断结果被归为每个维度的分数,因此低分可以被追溯到具体的失败检查. 我们利用BinEval框架评估了模型产出对图、图三覆盖和流畅度的信念。 我们使用DeepSeekV-4.1-Flash Xu等人(2026年)和GLM-5-3-Flash GLM-5-Team等人(2026年),思维残疾为LLMs法官. 我们没有让宾埃瓦尔框架产生二进制问题,而是向法官LLMS提供我们自己针对每个标准的问题. 对于每个问题,评价者给出了二进制输出,最后记录的分数是在信仰和流利情况下每个维度的总满意问题的平均值. 向法官提出的问题见表12和表13。 对于"覆盖",最终分数为每三分与总分之比为二分之和. GPTScore也是一种无参考度的度量衡,它根据预先训练的语言模型分配给它的可能性对生成的文本进行评分,并以指令为条件. 我们利用GPTScore来获得源图和任务指示生成输出的可能性. GPTScore的正式实施是通过Flan-T5,GPT-2,GPT-3和OPT家族模型进行测试的,然而,我们在非思维设置中使用了DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,因为它是一个较新的模型,与我们用于文本生成的LLMS相比属于不同的模型家族. BinEval和GPTScore的执行细节载于附录B。

The evaluation results from LLMs as judge for all the three datasets on Faithfulness and Coverage is presented in Table 4 and for WebNLG17 and WebNLG20 on Fluency in Table 11 . Both the evaluator LLMs have ranked the models similarly, with the prompted models being better than the fine-tuned models, which is not consistent with the ranking of models given by reference-based metrics, where the encoder-decoder model T5 is ranked the best in most scenarios. Another observation is that GLM-5.3-Flash as an evaluator, is more lenient than DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Faithfulness and Coverage and stricter on Fluency, so rankings and differences are comparable across judges, and absolute scores are not; Fluency is saturated and differs more between judges than between systems, so no conclusion is drawn from it in this paper. On careful study of per-question failures on the full WebNLG17 outputs on all the generator models, we observed that fine-tuned models (T5 and LoRA-tuned T5-Gemma2) separate cleanly from the prompted systems under both the LLM judges. The two fine-tuned systems have a faithfulness failure on 12% to 23% of their outputs, and the four prompted systems on 2% to 10% (Table 5 ). A T5 or T5-Gemma2 output failure is usually a whole-output corruption, whereas a prompted model output usually fails on a single question. Among failed outputs, the share of all-question failure is 32% to 46% for the two fine-tuned systems and 11% to 27% for the four prompted ones. In counts: 146 and 198 outputs under DeepSeek for T5-large and T5-Gemma2, against 20 to 46 for the prompted systems. The two judges agree with each other more on the fine-tuned systems (Cohen’s kappa 0.62 and 0.68 over all binary verdicts for each model’s outputs) compared to the prompted ones (0.32 to 0.45). Where real errors exist, the judges converge; where they do not, each judge raises its own spurious flags. Also, the errors grow with graph size, and much faster for the fine-tuned models. From graphs of one or two triples to graphs of four or more, the share of outputs with a faithfulness failure goes from 8% to 26% for T5-large and from 9% to 38% for T5-Gemma2 under DeepSeek, and the share with a missing triple from 3% to 27% for both (Tables 16 and 17 .
GPTScore on the other hand has remained largely inconclusive as clear from the Table 15 .

blocks.en: 6.3 Validation against human annotations (RQ3, RQ4)
blocks.zh: 6.3 对照人的说明进行验证(RQ3,RQ4)

blocks.en: To establish what the LLM judge scores measure, one author annotated the outputs of T5-large and Nemotron-3-Ultra on the same 110 WebNLG17 graphs (with graphs containing triples 1 to 7, with at least five graphs of sizes 6 and 7), answering the three Faithfulness questions provided in Table 12 for each output and recording omitted triples. A second author then analysed every failed question and every LLM judge verdict that the annotator had passed, with the judges’ explanations visible; the decisions of the second author are final. According to the annotator, the failed questions fall into three kinds: Unsupported Elaborations (where the text adds plausible content that the graph does not state, failure of question 1 from Table 12 ), Entity Corruptions (misspelt or altered entity names and values, failure of question 2), and Contradictions (wrong or reversed relations, failure of question 3). Contradictions and entity corruptions occur only in T5-large outputs on the annotated sample (10 out of 110 outputs); DeepSeek detects all ten such failed questions and GLM eight. Unsupported Elaborations are the only failure cases of Nemotron-3-Ultra (9 of 110 outputs) and also occur in T5-large (3 out of 110 outputs) on the annotated sample; the judges flagged only one of these twelve while on the full dataset, the judges do catch some unsupported elaborations of one specific kind: a relation reworded with more meaning than the graph gives (for example, the output mentioning “plays for” for the relation "club", “county seat” for relation "largest city", and “official language” for relation "language"; etc.). At the output level, agreement with the adjudicated labels on T5-large is Cohen’s kappa 0.56 for DeepSeek (precision 11/21, recall 11/14) and 0.75 for GLM (11/14, 11/14) (Table 6 ). For graph triple coverage, the judges reproduce the annotator’s omissions at the level of the individual triple. On T5-large, which omits at least one triple in 11 of 110 outputs (mostly on graphs with four or more triples), DeepSeek recovers 10 and GLM 9, naming the same missing triples; their remaining flags are triples that were rendered incorrectly or expressed without a qualifier. Nemotron-3-Ultra omits a triple once, and both judges find it. The coverage scores in the judge figures can be read as triple omission rates. By the annotator’s standard the two systems have flagged Faithfulness failure in a similar share of outputs (14 and 9 of 110, paired sign test p = 0.36) but of entirely different kinds. The LLM judge Faithfulness scores should therefore be read as rates of hard faithfulness errors (contradiction and entity corruption), on which the prompted models are clearly better. Table 6 summarises the validation.

blocks.en: 6.4 Agreement between metrics (RQ2)
blocks.zh: 6.4 衡量标准之间的协议(RQ2)

blocks.en: Since the evaluation metrics used in this work assess generated text from different perspectives, it is important to analyse them in detail. Figure 6 present the Spearman correlation between the evaluated metrics for all six model outputs on WebNLG17 dataset. Overall, the reference-based NLG metrics exhibit a strong correlation among themselves with correlation of 0.62 to 0.92, for all model outputs which drops to 0.36 to 0.06 with LLM judge: BinEval1 (Faithfulness using DeepSeek-V-4.1-Flash) with BLEURT correlating the most with it, mostly in case of fine-tuned models. The same goes for BinEval2 (Faithfulness using GLM-5.3-Flash). The two judge LLMs also correlate best with each other on fine-tuned models with correlation of 0.74 on T5-Gemma2 and of 0.67 on T5-large with least corelation value on GPT-5-mini. In addition to correlation between metrics, Table 14 presents some examples where the surface-level metrics report a low score compared to semantic metrics because of the difference in textual framing, thus showing that the surface-level metrics, as commonly used alone for evaluation, were never sufficient to assess the correctness of the generated text.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we show that the prompted decoder-only models stand close to, and in some cases (like on WebNLG20) even slightly ahead of, the fine-tuned baseline T5-large on reference-based evaluation, while clearly outperforming it on source-grounded evaluation; the LoRA-tuned encoder-decoder behaves like a fully fine-tuned T5 model on both. To better understand this, we examined how our LLM-based BinEval evaluations relate to the reference-based metrics: BinEval scores do not correlate strongly with the reference-based metric families, which themselves correlate well with one another across all model outputs. We find that the judges reproduce human judgements closely on hard failure cases such as contradictions and entity corruption, but often fail to flag unsupported elaborations in the output text. Despite this latter limitation, the BinEval evaluations still support our conclusions that the prompted models used in this study contain fewer contradictions and triple omissions than the fine-tuned baseline. We also got evidence that the fine-tuned models become more prone to graph-grounded errors as the graph size increases compared to the prompted models. Current benchmarks have graphs of at most seven triples and texts of a few sentences; as the size and complexity of the input subgraphs increase, we expect both factual errors, omissions and ungrounded elaboration to become more prevalent, making their systematic detection essential, and no current automatic evaluation is able to reliably detect the latter. Thus, evaluating report-scale generation needs a larger aligned dataset and evaluation protocols that detect ungrounded elaboration.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们显示被激发的解码器唯一的模型站得近,在某些情况下(如WebNLG20上)甚至略高于参考评价上微调的基线T5大,同时在基于源的评价上明显优于它;Lora-tuned编码器-解码器在两者上的行为都像一个完全微调的T5模型. 为了更好地理解这一点,我们审查了我们基于LLM的BinEval评价与基于参考的衡量标准的关系: BinEval的分数与基于参考的计量系统没有密切关联,后者本身在所有模型产出中彼此间关系良好。 我们发现,法官们在诸如矛盾和实体腐败等严重失败案件中密切地重复了人类的判断,但往往没有在产出文本中标出未经支持的阐述。 尽管存在后一种限制,但BinEval评价仍然支持我们的结论,即本研究中使用的激励模型的矛盾和三重遗漏比微调基线少。 我们还有证据表明,微调模型比起被激发模型,随着图表大小的增大,更容易遭受以图表为根据的错误. 目前的基准图最多有七分之三,并有几句话的文本;随着输入子图的大小和复杂性的增加,我们期望事实错误、遗漏和无根据的阐述都更加普遍,这使得系统发现它们至关重要,目前没有任何自动评价能够可靠地发现后者。 因此,评价报告规模生成需要更大的统一数据集和评价协议,以发现无根据的阐述。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Our experiments results on T5 fine-tuning are not numerically identical to all the published values because of differences in evaluation protocol(Table 8 ). The details of our evaluation settings is provided in Section 5.3 . Our experiments on decoder-only models rely on single generation runs per model, so we cannot rule out variance across repeated samples. Our fine-tuned pole is also limited to T5-large and a single LoRA-tuned model; extending fine-tuning to a decoder-only architecture is left to future work. For human evaluation, a single annotator rated outputs, with a second author adjudicating every disputed verdict with the LLM judges’ explanations visible; this visibility may have anchored the second author’s adjudication toward the judges’ reasoning rather than serving as a fully independent check. The annotation also covered only one prompted system (Nemotron-3-Ultra) and the Faithfulness and Coverage dimensions, leaving Fluency unannotated. With only 110 graphs annotated from a total of 1862 samples on WebNLG17, the resulting counts are small, and the reported agreement statistics carry wide confidence intervals. Because errors missed by both the annotator and the judges remain undetected, the judge recall figures we reported should be interpreted as upper bounds rather than exact values. We also want to highlight that the benchmark datasets WebNLG17, WebNLG20 and DART are not independent of each other by construction because DART incorporates WebNLG17 data directly, and WebNLG20 extends WebNLG17’s underlying triple set, so we cannot rule out the possibility of dataset memorization by judge LLMs. Finally, as we mentioned earlier, GPTScore using DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has remained inconclusive; this study does not include an analysis of the reason for the same.
blocks.zh: 由于评价协议的不同,我们在T5微调方面的实验结果与所有公布的数值在数字上并不相同(表8)。 第5.3节详细介绍了我们的评价设置。 我们对解码器模型的实验 依赖于每个模型的单代, 所以我们不能排除 重复样本的差异。 我们的微调杆还被限制在T5大和单一的LORA调制模型;将微调扩大到只解码器的架构则留待未来工作. 就人的评价而言,一个书记员对产出进行评分,第二个书记员用LLM法官的解释来裁定每个有争议的判决;这种能见度可能使第二个书记员的裁决建立在法官的推理之上,而不是完全独立的检查。 注释还只涉及一个提示系统(Nemotron-3-Ultra)和信仰和覆盖维度,使得Fluency没有说明. 由于WebNLG17上总共有1862个样本,只有110个图作注释,结果的计数很小,所报告的协议统计具有广泛的置信间隔. 由于注释员和法官都忽略了错误,因此法官回顾我们报告的数字应被解释为上限,而不是准确的数值。 我们还想强调,基准数据集WebNLG17,WebNLG20和DART并不是通过构建而相互独立的,因为DART直接融合了WebNLG17的数据,而WebNLG20扩展了WebNLG17的基本三重集,因此我们不能排除法官LLLMs进行数据集计量的可能性. 最后,正如我们先前提到的那样,使用DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash的GPTScore仍然没有定论;本研究不包括对同样原因的分析。

blocks.en: GPT-5-mini consistently produces fluent text; however, the quality of the generated output is highly dependent on the prompt provided to the model. We initially employed the prompt Generate text from graph:{ g ​ r ​ a ​ p ​ h graph },” following the approach of Yuan and Färber (2023) for the WebNLG dataset. During preliminary experiments, we observed several recurring issues. The model frequently failed to recognize that "<H>", "<R>" and "<T>" were structural markers and instead interpreted them as literal entity identifiers, referring to the head, relation, and tail entities as "Entity H", "Entity R" and "Entity T", respectively. Moreover, the model produced text that does not make sense semantically but is consistent with the order of entities present in the graph. In addition, the GPT-5 models occasionally produced explanatory comments or intermediate reasoning along with the generated output. These observations are consistent with the error analysis reported by Yuan and Färber (2023) . Examples of these errors are presented in Table 7 . To mitigate these issues, we incorporated explicit instructions addressing these common failure cases within the detailed prompt shown in Table 10 . We observed that the revised prompt was effective in eliminating these recurring errors from the generated outputs.

blocks.en: Appendix B Bineval and GPTScore details
blocks.zh: 附录 Bineval 和 GPTS 核心细节

blocks.en:
In this section, we provide the details of BinEval score and GPTScore evaluation. BinEval Score has been used to judge the outputs of six models on three datasets as mentioned earlier, for semantic faithfulness of the generated text with the graph, graph triple coverage in text and fluency of the text. For evaluating semantic faithfulness, we used the following system prompt: Evaluation input format: The input graph is a knowledge graph represented as a sequence of one or more linearized triples.Each triple has the following structure: <H> Head <R> Relation <T> Tail where "<H>", "<R>", and "<T>" are literal strings that indicate the head, relation, and tail of the triple, respectively. The input graph is followed by a candidate output text that is generated from the graph. Your task is to evaluate whether the output text accurately reflects the information in the input graph by answering the provided questions. For each question, you should provide a JSON object with two fields: "satisfied" and "explanation". The "satisfied" field should be a boolean value indicating whether the
output text satisfies the question, and the "explanation" field should be a string providing a brief explanation of your answer. Judge the text only according to the respective question." . For the dataset Dart, we made some changes in the prompt to help the evaluator LLM understand the Dart dataset graph format better: Evaluation input format: The input graph is a knowledge graph represented as a sequence of one or more linearized triples.Each triple has the following structure: <H> Head <R> Relation <T> Tail where "<H>", "<R>", and "<T>" are literal strings that indicate the head, relation, and tail of the triple, respectively. Some graphs are derived from tables and may contain special bracketed markers instead of real-world entities. "[TABLECONTEXT]" represents the data table or record as a whole - it is not a specific entity and should never be treated as one. When the relation is "[TITLE]" or "[title]", the triple’s tail is the title of the table or record, not a literal string that must appear verbatim (e.g. <H> [TABLECONTEXT] <R> [title] <T> A Severed Wasp; means the table’s title/subject is "A Severed Wasp" - this is content the candidate text may describe). The input graph is followed by a candidate output text that is generated from the graph. Your task is to evaluate whether the output text accurately reflects the information in the input graph by answering the provided questions. For each question, you should provide a JSON object with two fields: "satisfied" and "explanation". The "satisfied" field should be a boolean value indicating whether the output text satisfies the question, and the "explanation" field should be a string providing a brief explanation of your answer. Judge the text only according to the respective question. The prompt is accompanied with three questions and corresponding violation examples presented in table 12 . The violation examples in the prompts are not taken from the test sets. For the evaluation of fluency of the outputs, we used the following prompt to define the task: Evaluation input format: You will be provided a candidate output text. Your task is to evaluate whether the output text is in fluent English by answering the provided question. For each question, you should provide a JSON object with two fields: "satisfied" and "explanation". The "satisfied" field should be a boolean value indicating whether the output text satisfies the question, and the "explanation" field should be a string providing a short explanation of your answer. Judge the text only according to the respective question. The three questions and corresponding violation examples are presented in table 13 . For Coverage, we converted the input graph into an ordered list of triples as input to the evaluator and for each triple, asked the evaluator to answer the question " Does the text describe the information present in this triple? " and recorded the binary answer for each triple and obtained the ratio of sum of the scores to the total triples.
For GPTScore, we evaluate the likelihood scores for the generated text given the input graph and instruction prompt describing the task: "Generate a natural-language text description of the following knowledge graph" .

"满意"字段应该是一个布尔值,表明输出文本是否满足了问题,而"解释"字段应该是一个字符串,对你的答案提供简短的解释. 只根据各自的问题判断案文。 三个问题和相应的侵权事例见表13。 为了涵盖范围,我们把输入图转换成一个有条不紊的三重体清单,作为对评价者的投入,每三重体,我们请评价者回答一个问题: " 案文是否描述了这三重体中的信息? ",并记录了每三分之一的二进制回答,并获得了分数和总分之比.
